t: Nothing stands here now, but this was the site of St Olave's Church, on the south side of Silver Street, off Wood Street. It was dedicated to St Olaf, a Norwegian Christian ally of the English king Ethelred the Second. The Great Fire of London destroyed it in 1666, and it was never rebuilt. Two people were born in its parish. Agnes Cowper was a servant and vagrant whose life was recorded in detail as neighbouring parishes tried to avoid having to support her. Matthias Sention, born in 1601, later became a Connecticut settler.
